metric.why: The ride-through chain is only as real as its weakest measurement. Batteries age silently, and fuel contracts measured in days assume deliveries that a regional emergency interrupts.
metric.metric: UPS battery health and generator runtime
metric.definition: Battery state of health and remaining runtime under current load, and on-site fuel measured in hours of generator operation at load.

reading.body:
Aging UPS batteries and limited on-site fuel are the most common points where data center redundancy fails in practice, because both degrade between the moment of installation and the moment they are needed.

Battery state of health declines silently. A battery that tests within spec under a light periodic check can still fail to sustain load during a multi-minute outage. Fuel measured in days of runtime assumes that deliveries arrive on schedule, and a regional emergency is precisely the condition that disrupts both the grid and the supply chain simultaneously. The ride-through chain, from utility failure through battery bridging to generator sustain, is only as strong as the weakest of those three links, and two of the three are time-dependent in ways that static procurement decisions do not capture.

For AI infrastructure specifically, the stakes are higher than for general enterprise computing. Dense GPU clusters draw sustained, near-peak power continuously rather than in bursts, which means batteries discharge faster and generators run closer to their rated limits. Neither the battery health figure nor the fuel-hours figure in isolation tells an operator whether the site can survive a prolonged outage under actual AI workload, as opposed to the load profile assumed at design time. The data covers operational measurement, not design margins, capacity planning, or the upstream question of how grid instability affects outage frequency in the first place.
